summary: Ground L-4 cab built 1931-32 on Council Bluff, Skamania County; gone by the 1960s or earlier (sources differ); no remains described; hike from Council Lake.

facts.design: L-4 cab on a ground house with a gable roof
facts.status_note: Cab removed or destroyed; sources differ on whether it went in the 1950s or the 1960s

access.note: National Forest land reached on foot; Willhite describes a 1.5-mile hike that can start at Council Lake Campground

visit.trail_note: About 1.5 miles and 950 feet of climbing per Willhite; the old road now makes a hike

Willhite: likely abandoned in the 1950s; decade only, no exact year given
Firetower.org: removed in the 1960s; decade only, no exact year given
A survey party reported it demolished; destruction date unknown, before 1964

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firetower.org says the L-4 cab was removed in the 1960s; FireLookout.com says destroyed in the 1960s; Willhite says likely abandoned in the 1950s and destroyed before 1964. The story reports the disagreement without choosing one.
Firetower.org and FireLookout.com say 1930s; Willhite and the July 1931 newspaper item give construction in 1931 and 1932. The story uses the more specific dates.

notes_for_editor: Brief access was unknown; Willhite describes a hike from Council Lake Campground on National Forest land, so access is set to public. Fate dates conflict (1950s vs 1960s) and the story reports both. No source describes what remains on the summit; Willhite has 2018 drone photos that were not viewed as images. Brief record otherwise matches sources (elevation, status, agency).
